description: The VECTOR VALUE itself, as the whole function family depends on it: the cast's conversion rules and errors, 32-bit element widths, display text, column storage round-trip, and the ordinary SQL operations. Every expectation is measured on a real Snowflake account. A FLOAT vector displays each element with six decimals, [1.000000,2.000000,3.000000], where the INT form is [1,2,3], and pi lands at float32 width, reading 3.141593. INT elements are 32-bit and WRAP: 2147483648 becomes -2147483648 and 2^53+1 becomes 1, the low 32 bits. The cast rejects a wrong-length array, non-real elements and fractional elements for an INT vector, each with its own sentence, while whole-valued decimals DO convert. A vector casts only to its OWN type: the identity cast is the unchanged vector and any other element type or dimension is 'Invalid argument types for function CAST'. TYPEOF reports the bare family name VECTOR. A stored column round-trips and every function still works over it. Vectors compare, GROUP BY, DISTINCT and ORDER BY, and flow through CASE, COALESCE, UNION and UDF bodies - but a vector EXPRESSION is refused in a VALUES clause, exactly as for the semi-structured types, so INSERT ... SELECT is the supported route. Converted 1:1 from functions/vector/VectorValueSemanticsTest (now retired); every vector is read as a bare cell, as recorded in functions-vector-avg - TO_VARCHAR over a VECTOR is refused, a UDF's VECTOR result included - and the Java's assertRejected becomes the exact live message in all nine cases.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE vec_store (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
SELECT v FROM vec_store WHERE id = 1
SELECT VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE(v, [1,2,3]::VECTOR(FLOAT,3)) FROM vec_store WHERE id = 1
SELECT VECTOR_NORMALIZE(v) FROM vec_store WHERE id = 1
SELECT VECTOR_TRUNC(v, 2) FROM vec_store WHERE id = 1
SELECT IS_VECTOR(v) FROM vec_store WHERE id = 1
SELECT v FROM vec_store WHERE id = 3
CREATE TABLE vec_cmp (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vec_cmp WHERE v = [1,2,3]::VECTOR(FLOAT,3)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT v FROM vec_cmp)
SELECT LISTAGG(c, ',') FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM vec_cmp GROUP BY v ORDER BY c DESC)
SELECT v FROM vec_cmp ORDER BY v LIMIT 1
SELECT CASE WHEN TRUE THEN [1,2,3]::VECTOR(FLOAT,3) ELSE NULL END
SELECT [1,2,3]::VECTOR(FLOAT,3) AS v UNION ALL SELECT [4,5,6]::VECTOR(FLOAT,3)
